title: Boneless Chicken Wings with Hot Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Boneless chicken wings coated in a hot sauce are a popular snack item often served in bars and fast‑food restaurants. The chicken meat is tender, while the sauce adds a bold, spicy kick.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Boneless wings are easier to eat because they don’t require bone removal.
Hot sauce is usually made from chili peppers, vinegar, sugar and spices.
In the US they are commonly called "boneless wings" and come with a variety of sauces.
Chicken wings are a staple food during sports broadcasts.
There are many sauce variations: from classic Buffalo to Asian Sriracha.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat when prepared properly
items.content: If baked or grilled without excess oil, boneless wings remain relatively low in fat.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken contains niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: The product provides phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bones and immunity.

items.title: Capsaicin may boost metabolism
items.content: Chili peppers contain capsaicin, which can slightly increase thermogenesis.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Hot sauces often contain a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Spicy sauce can irritate the stomach
items.content: People with gastritis or ulcer disease should limit consumption.

items.title: Calorie density when fried
items.content: If the wings are deep‑fried, their calorie and fat content rise significantly.

items.title: Sugar in some sauces
items.content: Certain sauce recipes add sugar, increasing the product’s glycemic index.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wings can be served hot as a standalone snack, with celery or carrot sticks, or as part of combo meals. They are hand‑friendly and are often enjoyed with extra dipping sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked wings in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Frozen wings keep for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before eating.
